subject: Hosted API evaluation — quickstart & rate limits (Skyline AI)
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Kyle O'Neill <kyle@skylineai.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@skylineai.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API evaluation — quickstart & rate limits (Skyline AI)

Hi Kyle / Priya,

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier — appreciate you walking through the Skyline LLM use case. Per our call I wanted to capture the quickstart path for trying Hosted, plus answers on endpoints and rate limits so you have a clear pilot plan. High-level: a hosted eval should let you validate latency and cost for your document-summarization flow without any infra commitment.

Quickstart (what we recommend for a 2-week eval):
- Provision a guest API key (no infra changes) — I'll share the keys and a Postman collection.
- Test two endpoints: /v1/generate (streaming enabled) and /v1/embeddings for similarity pipelines.
- Start with 1k daily requests (50 concurrent) and a 128-token generation profile to emulate your POC. We'll provide example client configs in the attached quickstart doc.

Rate limits & quota:
- Default sandbox: 60 requests/minute, 10 concurrent streams. We can temporarily raise to 300 req/min and 50 concurrents for pilot with a short request to support.
- Per-token billing for hosted: will show estimated monthly token cost in the attached spreadsheet based on the sample traffic we discussed.

Data & retention:
- Hosted evaluation keeps request content encrypted in transit and at rest; you can opt-out of retention so logs are not persisted beyond 24 hours. If you need VPC/private deployment we can discuss Dedicated/Private next.

Next steps I propose:
1) I provide a guest API key + Postman collection and the quickstart markdown (attached).
2) You run the 2-week pilot with a dedicated evaluation rate limit bump — I’ll submit the request to support once you confirm target RPS.
3) We schedule a check-in mid-pilot to review latency percentiles and token burn.

Attachments: redwood-quickstart.md, skyline-usage-estimate.xlsx, endpoint-ratecaps.png

Any questions or anything I missed from the call? If this looks good I’ll push the rate-limit bump request and create the HubSpot trial record.

Cheers,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0133

From: Kyle O'Neill <kyle@skylineai.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@skylineai.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API evaluation — quickstart & rate limits (Skyline AI)

Thanks Alex — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifying questions before we kick off the pilot: 

1) Throughput: our production target for the summarization job is ~250 RPS bursts (300 concurrent) for short windows — would the temporary increase to 300 req/min and 50 concurrent streams you mentioned be sufficient to simulate that load? We mostly care about 95th/99th latency for 128-token outputs.

2) Data residency: we handle EU customer data; our compliance team wants to know if Hosted can restrict data to eu-west-1 for the eval (or do we need Private for that?).

3) Model pinning: can we pin to a specific model revision during the pilot and freeze auto-updates? We want repeatable outputs for regression testing.

Also — one of our infra people asked about how the KV cache behaves across requests (we typically send a multi-turn prompt across many short-lived requests). Happy to sync if it’s easier.

If it all looks good we’ll confirm a pilot start on Wed (3/17) and target a 2-week window.

—Kyle
Kyle O'Neill
Director of Engineering | Skyline AI
kyle@skylineai.com

Thoughts / proposed actions:

Alex

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Kyle O'Neill <kyle@skylineai.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@skylineai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 17:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API evaluation — quickstart & rate limits (Skyline AI)

Kyle / Priya — thanks for the questions. Short answers first, then proposed next steps.

1) Throughput: for the pilot we can raise concurrency to 300 concurrent streams and allow burst windows that emulate 250 RPS; this is a support-requested temporary change tied to the trial. Note: sustained production at that level is better served by Dedicated capacity (predictable tail latency & reserved GPUs).

2) Data residency: we can scope the hosted trial to eu-west-1 and enforce no-persistence for requests (24-hour deletion). For regulated EU data where you need KMS control or an audit boundary you’ll likely want Private.

3) Model pinning: yes — we can pin to a model revision for the pilot and disable automatic rev updates. I’ll include the model revision ID and a verification checklist in the quickstart doc.

KV cache: the runtime maintains KV cache per session; if you have many short-lived requests you can enable per-session tokens so the cache is threaded across requests. I’ve added a short note in the attached quickstart doc (redwood-quickstart.md).

Next steps (approved by Redwood):
- I’ll submit a support ticket to request the temporary rate-limit bump for your trial (300 concurrents, burst windows). If you confirm Wed 3/17 as a start date we’ll schedule the change to go live at 08:00 UTC that morning.
- I’ll share a pinned model revision and a Postman collection.
- Mid-pilot check-in: Mon 3/22 to review p95/p99 latency and token burn — propose a 30-min sync.
- Optional: if the pilot validates throughput and latency, Ben will follow up with a Dedicated sizing/commit recommendation and Lauren will propose pricing options.

Confirm the start date and I’ll proceed. In the meantime I attached the quickstart, the usage estimate, and a small diagram of endpoint rate caps.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
